author: Jawaharlal Nehru
prose_text_en: Writing from Naini Prison on October 26, 1930, Jawaharlal Nehru addresses his daughter, Indira, on her birthday. Unable to provide material gifts, he offers 'presents of the mind and spirit.' He advises against sermonizing, preferring open discussion. Nehru emphasizes the power of collective action, noting how ordinary people become heroes when they commit to a great cause. He highlights Bapuji's (Mahatma Gandhi) role in inspiring the nation and mandates honesty as a guiding principle: 'Never do anything in secret or anything that you would wish to hide.' He concludes by urging her to be a 'brave soldier' in India’s service.
summary_en: In this letter to his daughter Indira, Jawaharlal Nehru explains that while he is imprisoned, he can only send gifts of the mind and spirit. He encourages her to live a life of transparency, courage, and service to the nation. He stresses that true heroism arises when ordinary people unite for a noble cause, as seen in the Indian freedom movement led by Bapuji.
